thread:
carla: heads up, seeing recurring multi-node TP stalls around step ~120 on 8xA100. procs alive but entire job stops making progress. compute idle and allreduce waits spike.
ben: which config? tp/pp, microbatch, seq len distribution?
carla: tp=4 pp=1 microbatch=4 seq=1024 typical. started after recent kernel-selector tweak that prefers fused-batch kernels when median seq is small.
carla: small log excerpt:
```
[rank 2][step 119] allreduce wait enter timeout=30s count=512
[rank 3][step 119] kv-cache miss -> fallback_kernel selected
[rank 2] compute idle 14s
[rank 0] waiting at sync barrier
```
alice: that smells like per-rank kernel choice divergence. if one rank uses fused kernel and others fallback, launch geometry changes and collective timings can diverge.
dmitri: agreed. kernel_selector now uses local seq histograms; if kvcache is warm on some ranks only the local observed distribution differs.
carla: nvprof on a stalled run shows rank 1 launching fused_op, rank 2 launching fallback_op for identical op id; allreduce p99 shoots from ~80ms -> >1s and occupancy drops.
ben: quick mitigation ideas: 1) global/lockstep kernel decision per collective op, 2) leader ballot for kernel variant, 3) conservative selector for affected jobs.
carla: forcing KERNEL_SELECTOR=conservative removes stall but lowers tokens/sec ~18%.
alice: another contributing factor could be batching window misalignment across nodes. microbatch-to-shard mapping differs if leader batches slightly faster.
dmitri: repro plan: make tiny two-node 4-rank test. pre-warm kvcache on ranks 0/1 only to simulate skew, run with current selector and with lockstep flag and collect traces + nvprof.
carla: will add a vbench that dumps per-rank allreduce message sizes and seq-length bloom filter at op boundary to correlate.
ben: also instrument collective start times; if start time variance > N ms, runtime should prefer deterministic kernel variant for remaining ops in that batch.
carla: interim: enabling KERNEL_SELECTOR_LOCKSTEP=1 on dedicated infra for affected customers. eng-bot scheduled rollout:
eng-bot: rollout kernel-selector-lockstep to infra-dedicated-1 at 2026-03-22T02:00Z
carla: i'll run the repro and post artifacts (trace, nvprof tar.gz, small repro script) back here.
dmitri: i can help 1:1 tomorrow to gather traces. thanks.
alice: long-term we should centralize kernel decisions per-op or use a consensus of seq histograms across ranks to avoid local kvcache-induced variance.
carla: noted. posting updates after I have traces. (added participants: carla, ben, alice, dmitri, eng-bot)
